newsitem.title: USA: Goldman recommends caution on reinsurance sector.
newsitem.headline: Goldman recommends caution on reinsurance sector.

text.p: Goldman Sachs said it has become increasingly concerned about the outlook for the reinsurance industry and downgraded its rating on Transatlantic Holdings Inc to reduce its exposure to the sector.
In a research report Friday, analyst Thomas Cholnoky said price competition has begun to pick up and premium growth has begun to slow.
In addition to downgrading Transatlantic, Cholnoky recommended investors market weight the reinsurance group.
Transatlantic fell 2-1/4 to 68-1/4 in late trading.

Goldman removed Transatlantic from its recommended list and now rates it a moderate outperformer. Cholnoky said the company focuses on specialty reinsurance, which is better insulated from the overall industry trends, and therefore deserves an outperformer rating.

Goldman said it continues to keep Everest Reinsurance Holdings Inc on its U.S. priority list as its earnings growth outlook is significantly less reliant on industry fundamentals and more tied to restructuring and cost cutting initiatives.
But, he said, "we are becoming increasingly concerned about the erosion in the reinsurance industry fundamentals following second quarter industry results.
Increased price competition and slowing premium growth could put industry margins under pressure.

"We believe that these trends will persist through the balance of the year which could ultimately prove to be problematic for reinsurance industry underwriting margins," he said. "Although recent consolidations have reduced some of the structural capacity in the industry. This suggests rate pressure may exist for some time," he said.
